title: Check yourself: Defensive parsing, validation and the re-prompt

questions.stem: A reply arrives as a friendly sentence, then JSON inside a code block, then a closing remark. Which reading order does the page give?

options.text: Reject the whole reply, since extra words around the data are not allowed
options.says: Ruled out because the reader "repairs a harmless habit" of wrapping the data in words.

options.text: The first fence's body, else the span from the first brace to the last
options.says: The page's steps are to take the first fence's body, then "the span from the first `{` to the last `}`".

options.text: Strip only the leading sentence, then parse whatever text is left over
options.says: Ruled out because the steps start from the fence or the braces: "If the text has a code fence, take the body of the first fence".

options.text: Parse the last line alone, since data tends to follow the prose in a reply
options.says: Ruled out because the steps name no position for the data, only "Take the span from the first `{` to the last `}`".

questions.stem: A validator meets `true` where the schema wants an integer quantity. What does the page decide?

options.text: Accept it, since in many languages a truthy value counts as the number one
options.says: Ruled out because "A boolean is never a number or an integer".

options.text: Convert it to 1 and go on with the remaining checks of the field
options.says: Ruled out because the reader "does not repair a broken value", and the same holds for a value.

options.text: Report a separate problem for every constraint that the field carries in the schema
options.says: Ruled out because "A wrong type stops the checks of that value", so no further problem is added.

options.text: A single problem is reported for the value, and its other checks are skipped
options.says: The page says "A wrong type stops the checks of that value." and "`true` is not a quantity".

questions.stem: Which result ends the extractor loop without another call to the model?

options.text: A reply with a valid body but a total of zero, which breaks the minimum
options.says: Ruled out because the validator "returns a list of problems, each with a path", and the next call uses it.

options.text: A reply that was cut off because it ran into the token limit
options.says: The page says a reply at the limit has the action "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response", and that "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either".

options.text: A reply whose JSON is wrapped in a code fence with prose around it
options.says: Ruled out because "If the text has a code fence, take the body of the first fence", so the reply is read and not rejected.

options.text: A reply that quotes a sentence which the document never contained
options.says: Ruled out because a failed check leads to a repair: "the next call needs the whole conversation".

origin.section: Stop reasons that are not retried
